x: Another to gain early success in Belgrave colours is Jamie Stevenson. New to athletics but very talented, Jamie does not seem to know how 800 metre races are supposed to hurt.

It's refreshing to see someone like new member Jamie Stevenson (3rd from right) coming into the sport. Jamie, at 27, is relatively new to athletics and not being aware of where he should place in a race, runs to win.
Track man Jamie Stevenson ran well in the Walton Road Relay only to find that his team's next man off, Captain Colin Pearson, was nowhere to be seen.
In the A team Jamie Stevenson ran a stalwart first leg and Robin Brown confirmed Gordon Biscoe's predictions by running an immaculate 10th stage.

A fighting Jamie Stevenson boosted our middle distance points, running a personal best 800 metres in his first 1977 track race and in fact each of the middle distance events gave us at least 6 points, an improvement on how things stood at the end of last season.
The other first places came from Reg Hopkins and Arnold Bentt in the jumps and Jamie Stevenson in the 800m. Reg also set his best ever time in the 200m.
Top left: Lionel Mann leads the main bunch - Brian Gorman, Paul Roche, Leo Coy and Jamie Stevenson. Top centre: Charlie Manning attempts to hold on to Martin Best.

A second class standard medal went to Brian Gorman as a reward for turning in his fastest time for some years and Jamie Stevenson impressed onlookers by keeping well up the field throughout; no need for surprise, however, for Jamie seems to be a natural at any distance that he cares to tackle from 400 metres upwards.
Jamie Stevenson, suffering from a cold, handed over near the front but soon Ernie was loping along in the rear, coolly taking his pace from the other runners.
Jamie Stevenson placed 6th over 800m in 1:58.8 and Belgrave finished up third for the Club Trophy with 12 points to Thames Valley's 32 and Shaftesbury's 23.
A promising debut as a veteran came from Jamie Stevenson. You may remember Jamie as a very useful middle distance runner a decade or so ago; he should be a great asset to the relay squad.
